EFE(LOCAL) p.384 states 'District employees shall not use networking and booting (defined below) to accomplish multiple simultaneous use of a program without permission or unless the purchase agreement allows a specified multiple use of the single copy,' and bars using a purchased computer program as a 'master' to make copies. DH(LOCAL) p.221 adds employee technology-use rules: teachers may use cellular phones for business calls 'only during planning periods and other off-duty times,' phones must be 'off' during instructional time, and employees may not electronically record conversations or meetings without every participant's consent. CAUTION: there is no comprehensive acceptable-use policy, no email policy, and no internet-access policy for employees - the TASB CQ (Technology Resources) series is not included in this excerpt, which contains only the D (personnel) and E (instruction) series.

provision: Good cause is the governing standard for teacher discipline and dismissal: DFBA(LEGAL) p.159 'The Board may terminate a term contract and discharge a term contract employee at any time for: 1. Good cause as determined by the Board; or 2. A financial exigency...' (Education Code 21.211(a)), and may suspend without pay 'for good cause as determined by the Board'; DFAA(LEGAL) p.154 and DFCA(LEGAL) p.170 apply the same standard to probationary and continuing contracts, defining 'Good cause' as 'the failure to meet the accepted standards of conduct for the profession as generally recognized and applied in similarly situated school districts in this state' (Education Code 21.104, 21.156). DF(LOCAL) pp.151-153 lists 34 acts 'determined to be good cause for termination of an employment contract,' ending with 'Any other reason constituting good cause under Texas law.' Exception for a non-teacher subset: hourly/noncontract employees are at-will and 'may be discharged, with or without cause' (pp.73, 212).

provision: DEC(LEGAL) pp.102-108 is a full 'FEDERAL FAMILY AND MEDICAL LEAVE ACT (FMLA)' section (indexed on the DEC introductory page p.100 as 'Family and Medical Leave (FML) pages 4-11'): 12 workweeks in a 12-month period for employees with 12 months of service and 1,250 hours, birth/adoption/foster placement, care for spouse/child/parent, own serious health condition, notice, medical certification and recertification, maintenance of health benefits, end-of-term leave for instructional employees, reinstatement, and key-employee denial (29 U.S.C. 2611-2619). DEC(LOCAL) pp.116-117 adopts a 'rolling 12-month period measured backward,' requires concurrent use with medical and workers' compensation leave, caps spousal combined leave at 12 weeks, and sets a five-day advance request rule.

provision: No paid parental/maternity/paternity/bonding/adoption leave exists beyond accrued leave. Birth, adoption and foster placement are covered only by (a) unpaid FMLA - 12 weeks, DEC(LEGAL) p.103 and DEC(LOCAL) p.117; (b) unpaid temporary disability leave, for which 'pregnancy is considered a temporary disability' (DEC LEGAL p.102, Education Code 21.409); or (c) the employee's own accrued paid leave - DEC(LOCAL) p.115 lists as an allowed use of the five accrued local leave days '3. First-year care following the birth or adoption of an employee's son or daughter or the placement of a child with the employee for foster care, as provided by FMLA.' DEC(LOCAL) pp.113-121 enumerates every paid leave the District grants (five state personal days, five local days, two emergency days for home destruction, jury duty, professional activities, wartime military leave with pay) and no parental category appears; 'Any other leaves granted or days of absence shall result in a deduction of the daily rate of pay' (p.116).

provision: Compensation Guidelines Sec. VII 'Salary Credit for Experience' p.729: Creditable Years Service is 'evaluated for pay purposes at full value, one year for each year of creditable service. Newly employed teachers will be placed on a salary step on par with continuing teachers according to creditable years of experience,' determined by TEA rules, with 'A. Experience within Texas must have been at an institution fully accredited by the TEA' and 'D. Experience must be on a full-time basis for at least 90 school days'; Sec. VIII requires an official TEA Service Record, with the adjustment effective on the date of hire if filed within 30 days. Two provisions are expressly in-district: Sec. X p.730 - a former DISD teacher assistant who earns a standard Texas certificate 'must be credited with up to two years of full-time student instruction equivalency for salary increment purpose when employed as a teacher'; and Sec. XII - employees teaching 'either in the DISD or another school system' before wartime military service get salary credit as though teaching were uninterrupted. Step/CYS placement grid at p.670. CAVEAT: the manual states no rule distinguishing in-district from out-of-district Texas service - prior DISD service is credited through the same TEA CYS mechanism, at full value.

provision: Compensation Guidelines Sec.
